title: Hall of Fantasy
paragraphs: A supernatural anthology of eerie fantasy and horror stories, especially associated with writer-producer Richard Thorne.

Supernatural, fantasy and horror anthology associated with Richard Thorne. The frozen GRH snapshot mixes early KALL material, WGN/Mutual broadcasts, later rebroadcast/syndication airchecks, and at least one recording whose provenance is uncertain enough to require a recreation warning.

GRH documents the program through KALL local incarnation (1946 to May 4, 1947) on [[org|org.530c043ded979268|KALL]], WGN Chicago local revival (1949 to August 21, 1952) on [[org|org.06b4214104618161|WGN]], Mutual network run (August 22, 1952 to September 28, 1953) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Later rebroadcast/syndication cycle (October 5, 1953 to March 29, 1954) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Richard Thorne (writer on 17 recordings, performer on 7 recordings, producer on 6 recordings, radio adaptor on 4 recordings, director on 2 recordings, and author on 1 recording), Harold Turner (music on 4 recordings and organist on 1 recording), Leroy Olliger (director on 5 recordings), Carl Grayson (performer on 3 recordings), Harry Elders (performer on 3 recordings), Jim Ameche (performer on 3 recordings), and Wayne Dickenson (sound-effects artist on 3 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.06b4214104618161|WGN]] (originated at station), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include death, murder and lethal danger, supernatural forces, ghosts and the uncanny, curses, haunted objects and supernatural revenge, classic supernatural and horror literature, occult ritual, idols and dark magic, and monsters, creatures and nonhuman threats.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Regional local-radio anthology development, National Mutual supernatural anthology, Classic supernatural literature on radio, and Post-network rebroadcast and syndication cycle.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|gang-busters|Gang Busters]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|suspense|Suspense]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (1 shared credited people), and [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]] (1 shared credited people).
